subsystems.name: Design space definition
subsystems.role: Defines the volume where material is allowed and the loads and supports it must carry.
parts: CAD geometry of the design domain

subsystems.name: Simulation engine
subsystems.role: Calculates how a candidate shape responds to loads using finite element analysis (FEA).

subsystems.name: Optimization algorithm
subsystems.role: Iteratively redistributes material to find the lightest shape that meets the requirements.

subsystems.name: AI / machine-learning module
subsystems.role: Learns from past simulations to propose candidate designs faster or explore complex design spaces.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing constraints
subsystems.role: Ensures the optimized shape can actually be produced by the chosen process.
parts: draft or symmetry constraints for casting and moulding

subsystems.name: Post-processing and CAD export
subsystems.role: Converts the raw optimization result into a smooth, manufacturable solid model.

buildSteps.title: Define the design problem
buildSteps.detail: Specify the design domain, the loads it must carry, the fixing points, and the target mass reduction or stiffness.

buildSteps.title: Build the simulation model
buildSteps.detail: Mesh the domain, assign material properties, and set up the FEA so each candidate shape can be evaluated.

buildSteps.title: Run a baseline analysis
buildSteps.detail: Check the starting solid design to confirm the loads, supports, and material assumptions are correct.

buildSteps.title: Iterate topology optimization
buildSteps.detail: Run a density-based or level-set algorithm that removes material from low-stress regions and adds it along load paths, repeating until convergence.

buildSteps.title: Apply AI acceleration (optional)
buildSteps.detail: Train a surrogate model or GAN on previous simulation results to generate promising topologies quickly, then validate them with full FEA.

buildSteps.title: Enforce manufacturing constraints
buildSteps.detail: Add rules for the intended process — for example, a minimum feature size, an overhang limit for 3D printing, or draft angles for casting.

buildSteps.title: Validate and refine
buildSteps.detail: Run high-fidelity FEA on the optimized shape to check stresses, buckling, and fatigue, and adjust the design if needed.

buildSteps.title: Convert to CAD
buildSteps.detail: Smooth the voxel or density field into a clean solid model and export it for manufacturing.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture and test
buildSteps.detail: Produce a prototype — often by additive manufacturing because of the complex geometry — then test it and feed results back into the next iteration.

prerequisites.why: The optimization loop needs fast, reliable structural simulation to evaluate each candidate shape.
Density-based and level-set methods are the core mathematical engine that redistributes material.
Surrogate models and GANs can speed up or guide the search, but they are not yet standard in every commercial workflow.
Many optimized parts have organic shapes that traditional machining cannot easily produce; 3D printing is often used, but not always available for the required material or size.
Large FEA models and thousands of iterations require substantial compute resources.
The optimized result must be converted into a manufacturable model and linked to production tooling.

pathway.milestone: Topology optimization is standard in aerospace and automotive for brackets, housings, and structural parts, often paired with additive manufacturing.
pathway.unlocks: Lighter components that cut fuel use and material costs.

pathway.milestone: AI surrogates bring optimization time down from hours to minutes, allowing interactive generative design inside CAD tools.
pathway.unlocks: Engineers can explore many design variants in a single session.

pathway.milestone: Multi-physics and multi-material optimization becomes common, simultaneously handling structural, thermal, and fluid loads.
pathway.unlocks: Optimized parts for electric motors, heat exchangers, and battery enclosures.

pathway.milestone: AI models learn from manufacturing and in-service data to optimize parts for the whole lifecycle, including fatigue, repair, and recycling.
pathway.unlocks: Designs that are not just light but also durable and sustainable.
